data.title: Zhipu Releases GLM-5.4 Model on Coding Plan
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Jin10, an official operator at AI company Zhipu said GLM-5.4 is now available on Coding Plan, with new visual capabilities and stronger general coding capabilities. Over the past three months, the company advanced both Scaling Loop and model scale; users first saw changes brought by Loop Transformer. Quotas for V2, V3, and Team users have increased to 1.5 times. Users can access the model by setting its name to glm-5.4.

data.title: STOCKS | BHP Plans to Double South Australian Copper Output to 650,000 Tonnes Before 2040; Shares Rise 2.3%
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, BHP, the world’s largest publicly listed copper producer, announced on November 23 that it plans to double annual output from its South Australian copper operations to 650,000 tonnes before 2040. BHP’s Australian-listed shares rose about 2.3% to 52.6 Australian dollars as of publication.

BHP plans to increase its group-attributable annual copper production to 2 million tonnes by 2035, from about 1.4 million tonnes currently, an increase of about 43%. Its South Australian copper operations are expected to account for about one-third of the group’s planned additional copper output through 2035. The expansion will proceed in two phases: first raising annual output to about 500,000 tonnes, then to 650,000 tonnes before 2040.

BHP said the expansion will be funded mainly by operating cash flow from its copper business, which it expects to generate about $35 billion in cumulative attributable free cash flow by 2035. The company said long-term copper demand will be supported by electrification, renewable energy investment, digital transformation, and AI infrastructure. It also warned that existing copper mines cannot supply enough to meet future demand and that the global copper industry needs more investment and new capacity to address the long-term supply-demand gap.

data.title: Malaysia Palm Oil Industry Says CPO Tax-Waiver Opportunity Is Over
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Malaysia’s palm oil industry says the period when waiving the crude palm oil (CPO) export tax could have boosted shipments and eased stockpile accumulation has passed.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Maintains Fed Rate-Hike Forecast After 100-Basis-Point Tightening
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Chaoxiang Research, Goldman Sachs U.S. economist David Mericle said the bank’s U.S. Financial Conditions Index has tightened by about 100 basis points since early September, including more than 40 basis points last week. The move was driven mainly by lower U.S. equity valuations, rising 10-year Treasury yields and a stronger dollar. If conditions remain at current levels, Goldman estimates they would reduce U.S. year-over-year GDP growth in the fourth quarter of 2027 by 0.5 percentage points.

Goldman expects the Federal Reserve to raise rates by 25 basis points in December and by another 25 basis points in March 2027, despite market-driven tightening approaching the equivalent of a 100-basis-point rate increase. The bank cited elevated inflation and economic growth above its potential rate. Further market selloffs driven by concerns about declining AI capital spending could substitute for next year’s rate hike.

data.title: AI Data Center Boom Drives Billions Into Private Infrastructure
data.description: According to CNBC, infrastructure fundraising rebounded in the third quarter of 2026, with $62 billion raised across 21 funds, bringing the year’s total to $101 billion across 65 funds. Brookfield Asset Management raised roughly $50 billion in infrastructure commitments over the past year, including $26 billion for the latest vintage of its flagship strategy. The firm said $13 billion of that amount came after the quarter ended and that it was on track to exceed its $30 billion target in early 2027. Data centers, communications networks, renewables and energy storage have accounted for a growing share of infrastructure investment as AI expands. Goldman Sachs’ 2026 Global Alternatives Survey found that 43% of institutional investors had a more favorable outlook on infrastructure than a year earlier, while 49% of investors with a target allocation to the sector said they were under-allocated.

data.title: Shopify CEO Says Allegations Surrounding Jensen Huang’s Departure “Seemed Orchestrated”
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke said on David Senra’s podcast that the timing of allegations surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure “seemed orchestrated” and resembled a carefully planned effort to oust him. The allegations included an affair and an investigation potentially involving foreign intelligence operations. Lütke acknowledged he could be wrong and that Huang may have had an affair.

Lütke said some people could benefit from Huang’s departure but did not identify anyone. He called Nvidia board members “fools” and said their rushed decisions during the scandal risked turning the company into a traditional corporation. Nvidia previously said Huang voluntarily resigned because his disclosed conduct did not meet the company’s code of conduct, standards and cultural norms. Lütke said the bar for finding Huang unfit to lead should be higher.

data.title: Microsoft President Brad Smith Warns Risk of More Large-Scale Tech Outages Will Remain High
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing reports by Newsweek, CBS and other U.S. media, Microsoft President Brad Smith warned on the 22nd that the risk of large-scale technology outages could remain high in the coming months as organizations patch software vulnerabilities and upgrade aging infrastructure. Smith said the work would take longer than a few weeks and that information infrastructure worldwide was being upgraded.

Smith said artificial intelligence is speeding up the discovery of coding vulnerabilities, helping defenders address flaws but also enabling malicious actors to target systems. Organizations are deploying updates rapidly, leaving less time for testing; he said the rushed pace could itself cause instability, particularly in older systems. He urged users to install security updates, companies to modernize aging infrastructure, and organizations to coordinate with government agencies.

Recent technical failures in the United States have involved Microsoft cloud services, the Federal Aviation Administration’s air traffic control system, United Airlines and some banks’ network services. There is no evidence that the incidents are connected. Microsoft said on the 14th that it had completed repairs following a global service outage the previous week. The company attributed that outage to multiple servers unexpectedly going offline, overloading the remaining infrastructure and core processes on affected servers. Microsoft said the outage was not caused by malicious activity. The incidents have also prompted discussion about the global economy’s reliance on a small number of technology providers.

data.title: AI | Agon Raises $70 Million in Series A From Investors Including Roelof Botha
data.description: Agon, a UK startup making simulation software for the European defense industry, raised $70 million in a Series A round from investors including Roelof Botha, Sequoia Capital’s former head, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: U.S. Debt Ceiling May Need Nearly $5 Trillion Increase as Societe Generale Maintains $5,000 Gold Forecast
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, CIBC Capital Markets estimates the U.S. government could reach its $41.1 trillion debt ceiling as early as the end of February 2027. Congress may need to raise the limit by nearly $5 trillion to keep the government financed through the 2028 election.

Societe Generale says expanding U.S. deficits and debt could heighten concerns about the dollar’s credibility and support gold prices over the long term. The bank maintains its forecast for gold to reach $5,000 per ounce by the end of 2027, recommends buying on dips, and advises a 10% portfolio allocation to gold.

Despite recent pressure on gold from expectations of Fed rate hikes and rising Treasury yields, several institutions see signs of oversold conditions and dip-buying after a sharp pullback. They also view U.S. fiscal sustainability concerns as a long-term support for gold.

data.title: SIX Group Ramps Up Drive to Attract Growth Stocks to Its Listing Venues
data.description: According to Bloomberg, European bourse operator SIX Group AG is stepping up efforts to bring growth companies to its listing venues as it seeks to counter competition from private capital and US stock exchanges.

data.title: Japan Spot Power Price Reaches More Than Four-Year High on Cold-Weather Outlook
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Japan’s spot electricity price rose to its highest level in more than four years as forecasts of cold and snowy weather in parts of the country raised the likelihood of increased consumption of expensive gas.

data.title: Bitcoin ETF Outflows Accelerate, Removing a Key Source of Support
data.description: Investors are withdrawing money from U.S.-listed Bitcoin exchange-traded funds at a faster pace, removing a key source of support for the beleaguered cryptocurrency. According to Bloomberg, the pace of withdrawals is accelerating.

data.title: Hyperliquid BTC Perpetual Market Shows $5.02M Bid at $61,790
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Liquid247.xyz, a bid for about 81.26 BTC, with a notional value of approximately $5.02 million, was posted at $61,790 on Hyperliquid’s BTC perpetual market. The price was about 0.00% below the midpoint of approximately $61,791 at the time.

Across nearby order-book levels on the exchange, bids totaled approximately $9.50 million and asks $11.24 million. Sell-side depth exceeded buy-side depth by about $1.74 million, or 8.39% of total depth.

data.title: STOCKS | China's Three Major A-Share Indexes Turn Positive
data.description: China’s three major A-share indexes moved into positive territory. According to Odaily, the Shanghai Composite had fallen more than 1% during the morning session, while film and cinema, humanoid robotics, precious metals and CPO stocks led gains; more than 4,300 stocks rose across the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing markets.

data.title: AI | JPMorgan’s James Sullivan Sees Earnings Revisions as a Marker for Buying AI Stocks
data.description: According to Bloomberg, JPMorgan Co-Head of Global Fundamental Research James Sullivan said earnings revisions might help investors identify when to buy AI stocks. Nvidia sank 14% on Friday last week, while Anthropic fell 8.5% on its second day of trading and a gauge of chipmakers sank 11%.

data.title: India Private-Sector Activity Holds Steady as Manufacturing Strengthens
data.description: According to Bloomberg, India’s private-sector activity held broadly steady in November as stronger manufacturing offset softer services activity, a flash survey by HSBC Holdings Plc showed Monday.

data.title: Krystal Suspends Automated Contracts and Services After Detecting Suspicious Transactions
data.description: Krystal said it detected suspicious transactions originating from its system. According to Foresight News, the multichain liquidity management platform has suspended its automated contracts and services as a precaution while its team investigates. Krystal said its vault was not affected and user funds remain safe, and that it will provide further updates when more information is available.

data.title: Strategy's Bitcoin Stack Is 22% Underwater, Peter Schiff Says It's About to Blow Up
data.description: Strategy's Bitcoin holdings are about 22% below their average purchase price, while Peter Schiff says the company is “about to blow up.” Bitcoin traded at $59,045 on Sunday before recovering to $61,200 on Monday, about 28% below its level a month earlier, according to BeInCrypto. Strategy's average cost is roughly $75,400 per BTC, per SaylorTracker. MSTR closed Friday at $77.80, nearly 47% below its price a month earlier. Strategy's preferred stock, STRC (Stretch), closed at $93.60 on Friday, down from near its $100 stated value in mid-November; its variable dividend is currently set at 12% a year, making its effective yield about 12.8%. Schiff cited the yield on his latest podcast when he said Strategy was “about to blow up.” Strategy countered on X on November 20, 2026, that its net reserve was negative during the 2022 bear market, when one-third of its BTC was pledged as collateral, but is now $35 billion, with all its BTC unencumbered. The company also holds about $5.1 billion in U.S. dollar assets, which its third-quarter results say covers 3.4 years of payouts. In November, Strategy sold MSTR shares to fund STRC buybacks, adding shares without adding Bitcoin. Its next weekly filing will show whether buybacks continued with STRC near $93.

data.title: Morgan Stanley’s Bruna Skarica Sees Bull Case for UK Economy
data.description: Morgan Stanley Chief UK Economist Bruna Skarica sees grounds for optimism in improving productivity, potential benefits from AI adoption and resilience among UK households and businesses, Bloomberg reported. In an episode with host Merryn Somerset Webb, they discuss UK fiscal risks, drivers of the recent productivity improvement, whether AI could raise wages and living standards, and what a stronger economy could mean for UK markets over the next five years.

data.title: Libya Oil Output Falls After Pipeline Disruption at Biggest Field
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Libya’s oil production fell after a group disrupted a pipeline carrying crude from the country’s biggest field. The incident is the latest in a series of disruptions in recent months that have curbed supply from the OPEC member.
